Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 17, "heading": "CHAPTER 15. I MAKE ANOTHER BEGINNING", "previous_rows": [], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 15, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u017-h", "tag": "h2", "role": "heading", "text": "CHAPTER 15. I MAKE ANOTHER BEGINNING", "sha256": "711c7684e61c69567cec85bacd5b6e96673c50ccbe66925b568ccd61f2281950", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/h2", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": []}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0001", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Dick and I soon became the best of friends, and very often, when his day’s work was done, went out together to fly the great kite. Every day of his life he had a long sitting at the Memorial, which never made the least progress, however hard he laboured, for King Charles the First always strayed into it, sooner or later, and then it was thrown aside, and another one begun. The patience and hope with which he bore these perpetual disappointments, the mild perception he had that there was something wrong about King Charles the First, the feeble efforts he made to keep him out, and the certainty with which he came in, and tumbled the Memorial out of all shape, made a deep impression on me. What Mr. Dick supposed would come of the Memorial, if it were completed; where he thought it was to go, or what he thought it was to do; he knew no more than anybody else, I believe. Nor was it at all necessary that he should trouble himself with such questions, for if anything were certain under the sun, it was certain that the Memorial never would be finished. It was quite an affecting sight, I used to think, to see him with the kite when it was up a great height in the air. What he had told me, in his room, about his belief in its disseminating the statements pasted on it, which were nothing but old leaves of abortive Memorials, might have been a fancy with him sometimes; but not when he was out, looking up at the kite in the sky, and feeling it pull and tug at his hand. He never looked so serene as he did then. I used to fancy, as I sat by him of an evening, on a green slope, and saw him watch the kite high in the quiet air, that it lifted his mind out of its confusion, and bore it (such was my boyish thought) into the skies. As he wound the string in and it came lower and lower down out of the beautiful light, until it fluttered to the ground, and lay there like a dead thing, he seemed to wake gradually out of a dream; and I remember to have seen him take it up, and look about him in a lost way, as if they had both come down together, so that I pitied him with all my heart.", "sha256": "6c1e77cbd5f432c26e82fc2cdf243896d7caa6ac5114b164104d0f058dccad30", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[1]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0002", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "While I advanced in friendship and intimacy with Mr. Dick, I did not go backward in the favour of his staunch friend, my aunt. She took so kindly to me, that, in the course of a few weeks, she shortened my adopted name of Trotwood into Trot; and even encouraged me to hope, that if I went on as I had begun, I might take equal rank in her affections with my sister Betsey Trotwood.", "sha256": "4a52743e34507879c9e7726d0cd1a83cbc6a9fdf0815f22cfe180f38ed8f2b25", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[2]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0003", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Trot,’ said my aunt one evening, when the backgammon-board was placed as usual for herself and Mr. Dick, ‘we must not forget your education.’", "sha256": "02300973368227d749fec9a1453df1641978aeccfa13a681c87eb6b3c56e08dd", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[3]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0004", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "This was my only subject of anxiety, and I felt quite delighted by her referring to it.", "sha256": "536c51b42189b86a2162879180d34de7c00e593205dd2d9692a67e23d09965b7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[4]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0005", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Should you like to go to school at Canterbury?’ said my aunt.", "sha256": "1720f6d32f898587c5a787591c2833e5698ee3999bfac047cdbb66b819ef91cc", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[5]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0006", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I replied that I should like it very much, as it was so near her.", "sha256": "7ab20311f03dfb6b55e061b709204888678ab019140f8f063a36cad92ab41b44", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[6]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0007", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Good,’ said my aunt. ‘Should you like to go tomorrow?’", "sha256": "c5ddd915a3211530e47c00c0cb470a230f45b70fd2e6e844594bad4e68fd5021", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[7]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0008", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Being already no stranger to the general rapidity of my aunt’s evolutions, I was not surprised by the suddenness of the proposal, and said: ‘Yes.’", "sha256": "75ad1648083afcbf382763590df36f6e5984c6f21336e41558b5cd8f00cd4998", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[8]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0009", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Good,’ said my aunt again. ‘Janet, hire the grey pony and chaise tomorrow morning at ten o’clock, and pack up Master Trotwood’s clothes tonight.’", "sha256": "4c5be2032f65c5178b3cd9abb79f1b2c9b74ac2c11734887a383c43e4f680fa3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[9]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0010", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I was greatly elated by these orders; but my heart smote me for my selfishness, when I witnessed their effect on Mr. Dick, who was so low-spirited at the prospect of our separation, and played so ill in consequence, that my aunt, after giving him several admonitory raps on the knuckles with her dice-box, shut up the board, and declined to play with him any more. But, on hearing from my aunt that I should sometimes come over on a Saturday, and that he could sometimes come and see me on a Wednesday, he revived; and vowed to make another kite for those occasions, of proportions greatly surpassing the present one. In the morning he was downhearted again, and would have sustained himself by giving me all the money he had in his possession, gold and silver too, if my aunt had not interposed, and limited the gift to five shillings, which, at his earnest petition, were afterwards increased to ten. We parted at the garden-gate in a most affectionate manner, and Mr. Dick did not go into the house until my aunt had driven me out of sight of it.", "sha256": "cd90b8d945159098d59ac64213bd94add4b266465e7734aef385dd04d0416123", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[10]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0011", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My aunt, who was perfectly indifferent to public opinion, drove the grey pony through Dover in a masterly manner; sitting high and stiff like a state coachman, keeping a steady eye upon him wherever he went, and making a point of not letting him have his own way in any respect. When we came into the country road, she permitted him to relax a little, however; and looking at me down in a valley of cushion by her side, asked me whether I was happy?", "sha256": "a0a82ac368b6cf84d82478cee6ea20b47cb2bb354a4b8d2f029261e970e891c4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[11]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0012", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Very happy indeed, thank you, aunt,’ I said.", "sha256": "ec89da03001573f78e881e4c13d04478c26ede35a6b4010f6c0259fb56dd9596", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[12]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0013", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "She was much gratified; and both her hands being occupied, patted me on the head with her whip.", "sha256": "9c9b1de66164c48b691a60dab5d6b2512e2d76a83e61da3ef1efddafa3f1176f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[13]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0014", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Is it a large school, aunt?’ I asked.", "sha256": "5cae460588964b2a21e14d16da26ef29ba589d93079839af9e2947c5f1b380a3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[14]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0015", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Why, I don’t know,’ said my aunt. ‘We are going to Mr. Wickfield’s first.’", "sha256": "605a91f464420a5be969bb1309a2928288762f2f5448448e7c5612b2b735f185", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[15]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0016", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Does he keep a school?’ I asked.", "sha256": "12cb72852f43019d7b02edd90a9b8040a3d9a1937acd378414e8c5047034b2a5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[16]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0017", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No, Trot,’ said my aunt. ‘He keeps an office.’", "sha256": "bce39dc1be9bf80b094be0c676b99aebfa08d7328052da18ed1c173cf2b8ecb8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[17]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0018", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I asked for no more information about Mr. Wickfield, as she offered none, and we conversed on other subjects until we came to Canterbury, where, as it was market-day, my aunt had a great opportunity of insinuating the grey pony among carts, baskets, vegetables, and huckster’s goods. The hair-breadth turns and twists we made, drew down upon us a variety of speeches from the people standing about, which were not always complimentary; but my aunt drove on with perfect indifference, and I dare say would have taken her own way with as much coolness through an enemy’s country.", "sha256": "01783ed8e0712b3b2c0f5cb264d810724319a55f1f44f4b241a1cd75cc29a1c3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[18]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0019", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "At length we stopped before a very old house bulging out over the road; a house with long low lattice-windows bulging out still farther, and beams with carved heads on the ends bulging out too, so that I fancied the whole house was leaning forward, trying to see who was passing on the narrow pavement below. It was quite spotless in its cleanliness. The old-fashioned brass knocker on the low arched door, ornamented with carved garlands of fruit and flowers, twinkled like a star; the two stone steps descending to the door were as white as if they had been covered with fair linen; and all the angles and corners, and carvings and mouldings, and quaint little panes of glass, and quainter little windows, though as old as the hills, were as pure as any snow that ever fell upon the hills.", "sha256": "5bf7e6763c2fd3068e494a6c203ee456719f8ada5bd8a21803366ebb5e336077", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[19]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0020", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "When the pony-chaise stopped at the door, and my eyes were intent upon the house, I saw a cadaverous face appear at a small window on the ground floor (in a little round tower that formed one side of the house), and quickly disappear. The low arched door then opened, and the face came out. It was quite as cadaverous as it had looked in the window, though in the grain of it there was that tinge of red which is sometimes to be observed in the skins of red-haired people. It belonged to a red-haired person—a youth of fifteen, as I take it now, but looking much older—whose hair was cropped as close as the closest stubble; who had hardly any eyebrows, and no eyelashes, and eyes of a red-brown, so unsheltered and unshaded, that I remember wondering how he went to sleep. He was high-shouldered and bony; dressed in decent black, with a white wisp of a neckcloth; buttoned up to the throat; and had a long, lank, skeleton hand, which particularly attracted my attention, as he stood at the pony’s head, rubbing his chin with it, and looking up at us in the chaise.", "sha256": "0478bc5abf0e298e6dccfc13762dc72204a1639b514777413da1aa8d27d6eda0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[20]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0021", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Is Mr. Wickfield at home, Uriah Heep?’ said my aunt.", "sha256": "b735c28a5ccb1fc976b5f945a2b4d1ee2b6c0b2933c3b29104c4169e70840c2b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[21]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0022", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Mr. Wickfield’s at home, ma’am,’ said Uriah Heep, ‘if you’ll please to walk in there’—pointing with his long hand to the room he meant.", "sha256": "379ea0bfc0c7bbfc4c3768998818d3f3b3dac4ed11f67fd2c1b46d12afd6c601", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[22]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0023", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We got out; and leaving him to hold the pony, went into a long low parlour looking towards the street, from the window of which I caught a glimpse, as I went in, of Uriah Heep breathing into the pony’s nostrils, and immediately covering them with his hand, as if he were putting some spell upon him. Opposite to the tall old chimney-piece were two portraits: one of a gentleman with grey hair (though not by any means an old man) and black eyebrows, who was looking over some papers tied together with red tape; the other, of a lady, with a very placid and sweet expression of face, who was looking at me.", "sha256": "21681b7353158e893ebadabff5de5edf31e480ed0b73b739c339b7ef67ee2f7c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[23]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0024", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I believe I was turning about in search of Uriah’s picture, when, a door at the farther end of the room opening, a gentleman entered, at sight of whom I turned to the first-mentioned portrait again, to make quite sure that it had not come out of its frame. But it was stationary; and as the gentleman advanced into the light, I saw that he was some years older than when he had had his picture painted.", "sha256": "87928ba484b728ec2877bcc78f854f1977752a0e268ff43f930fed67a2b3d53f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[24]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0025", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Miss Betsey Trotwood,’ said the gentleman, ‘pray walk in. I was engaged for a moment, but you’ll excuse my being busy. You know my motive. I have but one in life.’", "sha256": "12d4d7454e3f4c8e5c9064f9d09a45459a4c14dc4567ed91138885d93f335620", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[25]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0026", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Miss Betsey thanked him, and we went into his room, which was furnished as an office, with books, papers, tin boxes, and so forth. It looked into a garden, and had an iron safe let into the wall; so immediately over the mantelshelf, that I wondered, as I sat down, how the sweeps got round it when they swept the chimney.", "sha256": "0edfe4ab4b9d87b2d2f51e6b179642e7821ebe8dbf4e63b052f80e3e8013e480", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[26]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0027", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Well, Miss Trotwood,’ said Mr. Wickfield; for I soon found that it was he, and that he was a lawyer, and steward of the estates of a rich gentleman of the county; ‘what wind blows you here? Not an ill wind, I hope?’", "sha256": "94263b25d2086d62bdffbd95e334b08b116112650ea8ef18bd23eaecbbcef318", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[27]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0028", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No,’ replied my aunt. ‘I have not come for any law.’", "sha256": "71897f08ed225bfc084eb4297a7e9cb0cfaa158d9465c12147b3e7a0c440a7da", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[28]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0029", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘That’s right, ma’am,’ said Mr. Wickfield. ‘You had better come for anything else.’ His hair was quite white now, though his eyebrows were still black. He had a very agreeable face, and, I thought, was handsome. There was a certain richness in his complexion, which I had been long accustomed, under Peggotty’s tuition, to connect with port wine; and I fancied it was in his voice too, and referred his growing corpulency to the same cause. He was very cleanly dressed, in a blue coat, striped waistcoat, and nankeen trousers; and his fine frilled shirt and cambric neckcloth looked unusually soft and white, reminding my strolling fancy (I call to mind) of the plumage on the breast of a swan.", "sha256": "f27f0db2ebd4ae1808a3d42ac18e471fd329c0983eed295cb55ca1cd702c5042", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[29]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0030", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘This is my nephew,’ said my aunt.", "sha256": "ab992bc42c05a85ac38b485362d8585513427cabd9d08a41a0dfa6bea3841377", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[30]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u017-b0031", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Wasn’t aware you had one, Miss Trotwood,’ said Mr. Wickfield.", "sha256": "e9eb674c6f36493d5fc61d011685f9286ada21f36514bc8078f66f1973ba1911", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[22]/p[31]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
